1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. e3 c5 4. Nc3 Nf6 5. Nf3 Be7 6. Bd3 $6 b6 7. O-O O-O 8. b3
Bb7 9. cxd5 exd5 10. Qc2 Nc6 11. a3 a6 $6 12. Rd1 $6 {Given that Black is now
basically forced to exchange on d4 and leave White with a pawn there, this rook
will be misplaced.} (12. dxc5 $1 {This was a last chance for Saint Amant to change
the structure and saddle Black with hanging pawns as a modern master would
prefer to do.}) 12... cxd4 13. exd4 h6 14. b4 Bd6 15. Re1 b5 16. h3 Rc8 17. Qb3
Qc7 18. Bd2 Qb6 {This is a good example of an odd habit of the players in this
game of shuffling around without any fear of losing tempo. The position is slow
enough that the tempo loss cannot be brutally punished.} 19. Be3 Ne7 20. Rac1
Nh5 $6 {For reasons that are very unclear to me, both players choose to place
their knights on the edge of the board.} 21. Qd1 Nf6 22. Nh4 $2 (22. Ne5 $14) 22...
Rc7 23. Qd2 Nh7 24. Qc2 $6 Nf6 25. Kh1 Ne8 $6 {A slightly odd move, but I guess
Black wants to put the knight on d6 and then c4, but it's tricky to get the
bishop to move away from d6.} 26. Nf5 $6 Nxf5 27. Bxf5 a5 $6 28. Qb3 $2 axb4 $1 29.
axb4 Rc4 30. Na2 $6 Nf6 31. Bd3 Qc6 $1 {Here's where things finally get spicy  $1 The
rook simply can't be captured now, but Staunton will soon convert this pretend
exchange sacrifice into a legitimate exchange sacrifice. In all cases, Staunton
will have great compensation if the exchange sacrifice is accepted.} 32. Qb2
(32. Bxc4 $4 dxc4 {and checkmate and the queen are threatened.}) 32... Qd7 33.
Kg1 (33. Bxc4 {Now the exchange sacrifice can be accepted, but Black's
compensation is incredible.} 33... dxc4 {threatening ...Qxh3+} 34. Kg1 Nd5 {And
the amazing knight, bishops, and pawn structure secure Black a major
advantage.}) 33... Nh5 $2 (33... Bb8 $15 {is one possible improvement.}) 34. Qd2 $2
(34. Bxc4 dxc4 35. d5 $13 {is much more unclear than before, largely because of
how unhelpful the knight is on h5, and because of that, White has achieved the
freeing d5.}) 34... f5 35. f4 $2 {This only makes the Be3 worse and gives Black
the e4-square and greater potential on the e-file.} (35. f3 $13) 35... Ng3 36.
Bxc4 {The exchange sacrifice is finally accepted.} 36... dxc4 37. Qb2 $6 Rf6 $6
38. Nc3 Ne4 $1 39. Re2 $6 Rg6 40. Rd1 $6 Nxc3 $1 41. Qxc3 Bf3 $1 $19 {Even after ...Be4,
Staunton would have a huge advantage due to the positional compensation, but
this move wins the material back, and now Staunton simply has a winning
advantage with a great bishop vs. a terrible one, better access to the open
e-file, and many weak pawns to attack.} 42. Rde1 $2 Bxe2 43. Rxe2 Qe7 $6 44. Qb2 $6
Re6 45. Kf2 Re4 46. Qa2 Kf7 47. g3 Qb7 48. Qa3 Re8 49. Qc3 $6 Qh1 50. h4 g5 $1 {An
excellent move, cracking things open just as Black's pieces are fully activated,
and White's remain tangled.} 51. Qe1 Qh2+ 52. Kf1 Qh3+ 53. Kg1 Qg4 54. hxg5
Bxf4 $1 {another nice little tactic} 55. Bxf4 Qxe2 56. Qxe2 Rxe2 57. gxh6 c3 58.
Kf1 Re4 59. Bc1 Kg6 60. d5 c2 61. Bd2 Rxb4 $1 {a little trick that White could not
prevent.} 62. d6 Rd4 63. Ke2 Rxd6 64. Ke3 Kxh6 65. Ke2+ Kg6 66. Ke1 b4 {Saint
Amant finally resigned.} 0-1
